hebdo.accroche: This week saw significant operational and industrial momentum in integrated air and missile defence across Europe and the Indo-Pacific alongside mounting geopolitical friction. Tensions surged in the Middle East around the Strait of Hormuz, while major powers accelerated hypersonic deployments, naval unmanned trials, and sovereign air defence architectures.

tendances.titre: Hypersonic and deep-strike weapons shift rapidly from testing to serial procurement
tendances.resume: Major powers are consolidating operational hypersonic strike capabilities. The US Air Force formally put the AGM-183A ARRW into production, expanding facilities in Alabama, while the US Navy broke ground on a dedicated Conventional Prompt Strike support depot at Yorktown. In Europe, the HYDEF interceptor programme expanded to 16 partner nations, and France committed to additional SAMP/T NG batteries equipped with Aster 30 Block 1NT interceptors.

liens.titre: USAF Orders ARRW Hypersonic Missile Into Production, The Same Weapon It Nearly Cancelled

tendances.titre: Accelerated integration of autonomous and lower-tier counter-drone architectures
tendances.resume: Militaries are urgently bridging the cost-per-kill gap against low-altitude drone saturation. Initiatives ranged from German AI-driven interceptors (Helsing Contra) and Rheinmetall Skynex passive sensor upgrades to Danish XENTA-M5 radars for Poland and rifle-mounted optical sights in Thailand. Concurrently, navies are moving counter-UAS capabilities onto uncrewed platforms, illustrated by US maritime sprint programmes and UAE EDGE trials.

liens.titre: EDGE integrates autonomous vessels and counter-drone systems in demo with UAE and US navies

tendances.titre: Allied sovereign air and missile defence networks adapt to high-intensity attrition
tendances.resume: Facing persistent missile barrages in Ukraine and the Gulf, allied planners are overhauling production and forward basing. The US established a permanent THAAD battery on Guam and selected Poland as a European Patriot PAC-3 maintenance hub, while approving 500 PAC-3 MSE missiles for Kyiv. Concurrently, regional players like Ukraine (Freyja) and Switzerland are pushing forward next-generation surface-to-air programmes.

tendances.titre: Indo-Pacific defence posture deepens via dispersed infrastructure and joint testing
tendances.resume: Allies in the Indo-Pacific are enhancing deterrence through operational dispersal and overseas testing agreements. Japan deployed its domestic Type-25 long-range missile launcher and secured missile firing access in Australia and India to bypass domestic space constraints. Simultaneously, the Philippines confirmed dispersed US access sites, AUKUS deployed USS Colorado to Western Australia, and China expanded power projection via a new 3,000-metre runway on Antelope Reef.

Despite parallel diplomatic mediation in Doha and Tehran, Houthi strikes into Saudi Arabia prompted Egypt to authorise defensive military support.
